page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The configuration includes 8 virtual CPUs, representing 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, and a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

This instance type includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It is network and EBS optimized, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. The combination of local high-speed storage and optimized network throughput supports workloads requiring fast data access and transfer rates without relying solely on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core CPU capabilities and memory bandwidth, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores falling in the middle 50% tier. However, single-core performance, including stress-ng single-core and gzip compression, is positioned in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory read and write speeds are average, while database operations and multi-threaded Geekbench scores show weaker relative performance. LLM inference tasks on medium models perform poorly, though text generation on small models achieves average speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5dn.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive applications that benefit from local NVMe SSD caching and enhanced networking. It is suited for workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, data analytics, and memory-bound enterprise applications where high memory capacity and local storage speed are prioritized over raw single-core compute power.
